existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: At Dunlop-house, on the 22d ult. Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan, Esq. to Miss Rachel Dunlop, daughter of the late John Dunlop of Dunlop, Esq.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: The notice explicitly names Rachel’s father. Dunlop-2144 is a checked compatible John of Dunlop, whose biography lists Rachel’s 1769 baptism. Newspaper date is 22 February; the maintained OPR citation gives 23 February. Preserve both pending original-register comparison. No mother is stated.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: Ayrshire list of game licences issued by the Sheriff’s Clerk between 27 July and 7 September 1802: Glasgow, Robert, Esq. of Montgreenan.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Contemporary use of the estate designation by 7 September 1802. It supports the 1802 Montgreenan association, without dating the purchase or establishing a family relationship.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: Game licences and deputations issued by the Sheriff Clerk of Ayrshire: Glasgow, Robert, Esq. of Montgreenan. A gamekeeper deputation also names Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan as principal.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: List covers 17 July–10 September 1806. Supports continued Montgreenan estate association; a deputation is an appointment of a gamekeeper, not kinship.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: County of Ayr, Ayr, 13 January 1808: Robert Morris of Craig, for himself, and as authorised by Mr. Glasgow of Montgreenan.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: The county meeting debated trial by jury in civil cases. Montgreenan’s Glasgow was represented by an authorised attendee; this does not place him physically at the meeting. Name, estate and chronology fit Robert-1076.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.paper: Aberdeen Journal, and General Advertiser for the North of Scotland
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: At Rome, on the 22d ult. Mrs Robertson Glasgow, of Montgreenan, of a daughter.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Reports a daughter born 22 November 1827 at Rome. Exact date, place and family designation support Charlotte Glasgow-3003’s recorded birth, but the notice does not give the child’s forename or the mother’s forename. Anne-2874 is the checked Montgreenan succession wife.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: County of Antrim: List of Persons applying to Register their Freeholds, under 10 Geo. IV, cap. 8. No. 2324: Alex. Glasgow, Lisnagaver — Lands — Kilconway, townland of Lisnagaver.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Original page now inspected; replaces the earlier access-blocked heading/extract assessment. This is an application, not proof of admission. No age or relative is stated. Alexander-951 and older Alexander-3904 remain compatible; conflicting age estimates prevent an automatic identification. The property is Lisnagaver; Kilconway is the barony.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: Hugh Allan v. Trustees of Robert Glasgow: the report calls Mrs Robertson Glasgow the late Robert’s natural daughter and first heir under his 1818 entail. It reports his death in 1827 and a supplementary entail and trust dated 23 June 1821, involving Seafield near Ayr.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Contemporary account of the 25 August hearing, independently supporting Anne’s daughter/heir description and the 1827 death year. It does not verify 19 April. Hugh Allan-8034, the profile-defined nephew, is a compatible appellant candidate; older Allan-8028 has no death recorded but would be 109. Neither identity is proved. These later deeds are distinct from the uninspected 1803 trust.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: House of Lords appeals: the report reproduces clauses of Glasgow’s settlement and says Lord Brougham recommended reversing the judgment below; judgment reversed accordingly. The heading appears to read Henry Allen v. Trustees of R. Glasgow.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Reports the Wednesday judgment, 2 September 1835. The estate, Seafield dispute and counsel identify the same litigation as the 26 August report, whose appellant is Hugh Allan. Preserve the discrepant heading; compare the original court papers before resolving the name. Reported deed extracts are not an inspection of the original deed.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: Auction advertised for 22 September at the Donegall Arms, Belfast: Larne corn and wheat mills, Kilwaughter corn mill, and Inver flour mills, with machinery, lands and lease interests in James Holmes & Co.’s possession.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Place-study evidence only. Different mill interests were held under the heirs of the Marquis of Antrim and under the Marquis of Donegall. The passage names no Glasgow surname and does not connect the Glasgow families to these mills or to a seventeenth-century glassworks.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: William Glasgow signed Belfast banks confidence notice dated 15 June 1820.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Compatible with Belfast grocer; signature alone does not establish that identity.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: William Glasgow removed from Rosemary Street to shop and stores at 34 Smith Street, Belfast; teas, sugars and groceries; notice dated 30 October.
existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.assessment: Documented Belfast grocer; no inspected bridge to Cookstown men.

existing_reviewed_newspaper_images_1800_.reading: William Glasgow received £5 from executors of Mrs Margaret Lynd, Cookstown, bequeathed for the Fever Hospital.
